The business leans on third party manufacturing in low cost Asian hubs, which is directly relevant when sourcing costs move in favor of US apparel brands.

Operations: Under Armour generates most of its revenue in North America at about US$2.8b, with additional contributions from EMEA at about US$1.2b, Asia Pacific at about US$700 million and Latin America at about US$200 million.

Under Armour gives you a way to consider the intersection of lower sourcing costs and a brand that is trying to repair margins and cut back on discounting. Supplier price pressure in Bangladesh and tariff refunds have supported gross margin, while management focuses on fewer SKUs, full price selling and growth in regions such as EMEA and Latin America. At the same time, the company is still working through losses, weaker footwear demand and higher tariff related costs, so any benefit from cheaper manufacturing is competing with other headwinds.
